ST-147 visual spec: /releases archive and release note detail

Phase 0 for #147. Static page: no filtering (decided 2026-10-11), so no JS. Both surfaces reuse shipped patterns; nothing here introduces a new visual format apart from the version in the tag column. Dark mode: toggle below.

1. /releases archive (desktop)

ARCHIVE BEHAVIOUR. Template: existing ArchivePage driven by an archivePage doc, slug releases, contentTypes [releaseNote]. List: DS List variant="register" via ContentList (same as /articles list mode). Tag column shows version (mono, uppercase) instead of the first category. Date shows releasedAt. Sort: releasedAt descending. No filter bar, no pagination until the count passes the archive page size (12): then the existing Pagination component, same as other archives. Summary text is not shown in the row (the List primitive has no summary slot); it feeds the meta description only. Empty state: the existing archive empty state. Row hover and focus-visible: as List today. No sticky, scroll-spy or sidebar on this page.

Body sections render with the same section renderer as articles, using the Subtle and Subtle Centered rich-text styles from #135. Text is carried over verbatim from the existing article.

← v0.35.0Next release →
DETAIL BEHAVIOUR. Shell: same as ArticlePage (detailPage grid, MetadataCard, PageSections, PageSidebar, ContentNav, citations when present). Differences from article: MetadataCard contentType is "Release note" linking to /releases; it shows version and releasedAt and hides reading time; no taxonomy chips unless the note carries categories or tags. Breadcrumb is the centred form that passed Visual QA in #135. Prev / next walk releasedAt order (previous = older). SEO: title, summary as description, canonical /releases/<slug>. JSON-LD type stays Article-like via the existing generator (decision: reuse, no new type).

4. Homepage "Recently shipped" card

No visual change. The existing release card gains an href to the matching note when one exists for that version, and renders as today when none does.
